# Veritone Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Announces Debt Exchange and Commitment Letter to Bring in New Financing


November 16, 2026 8:00am EST[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_76636d175ed5f9a92f63914adc4597c6/veritone/news/2026-11-16_Veritone_Reports_Third_Quarter_2026_Results_and_445.pdf)


## Related documents


[Earnings Webcast Audio](https://event.choruscall.com/mediaframe/webcast.html?webcastid=gyCNbqmh)


[Presentation PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_76636d175ed5f9a92f63914adc4597c6/veritone/db/2363/23366/presentation/VERI_-_3Q26_Investor_Presentation_Final.pdf)


[10-Q HTML](https://investors.veritone.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001615165-26-000010/veri-20260930.htm)[PDF](https://investors.veritone.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001615165-26-000010/0001615165-26-000010.pdf)[XBRL Zip](https://investors.veritone.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001615165-26-000010/0001615165-26-000010-xbrl.zip)


– *Completed exchange of $38.7 million principal amount of outstanding 1.75% convertible senior notes due November 15, 2026 (“Old Convertible Notes”) for $38.7 million principal amount of newly issued 1.75% convertible senior notes due December 15, 2026 (“New Convertible Notes”) and an aggregate of 1.6 million shares of common stock. The $6.8 million remaining principal amount outstanding of Old Convertible Notes will be paid at maturity on November 16, 2026 –*


– *Obtained commitment letter from Blue Torch Capital (“BTC”) for a new $40 million senior secured term loan, subject to certain conditions precedent, including a requirement for the Company to obtain additional financing. The Company is in discussions with certain parties, including its largest stockholders, for up to $25.0 million in additional financing which will satisfy such condition. If obtained, the Company expects to use a portion of the proceeds from these financings to repay the New Convertible Notes at maturity in December 2026 and the remainder for corporate and operating purposes –*


– *Announced strategic integrations and advancements with Box, Inc. (NYSE: BOX), Getac, and JustFOIA/MCCI connecting aiWARE’s award-winning public safety applications to accelerate our Public Sector iDEMS offering and existing sales and distribution –*


*– Q3 Revenue of $18.6 million, Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) of $55.9 million and Net Loss and Non-GAAP Net Loss of $19.2 million and $10.7 million, respectively –*


*– VDR sales pipeline of over $70.0 million with an active sales pipeline of up to $25.0 million –*


*– Completed next phase of restructuring, delivering over $18.0 million in annualized cost reductions since June 2026, or approximately 18% of annual Operating Expenses as compared to the trailing 12 months ended June 30, 2026 –*


*– Targeting additional cost reductions of $2.0 million to $7.0 million by year-end 2026, representing total annualized Operating Expense reductions of approximately 20% to 25% –*


IRVINE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--[Veritone, Inc.](https://www.veritone.com/) **(NASDAQ: VERI) (“Veritone” or the “Company”)** , a leader in building enterprise AI solutions, today announced results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


“We have spent the majority of fiscal 2026 taking actions to put Veritone in a stronger financial and operational position,” said Ryan Steelberg, President and Chief Executive Officer of Veritone. “With our newly announced convertible notes exchange and commitment letter, combined with our recent cost reduction efforts, we are on a clear path to greatly improve our financial position and ability to execute our operating model and product strategy. With the introduction of new products, and our expanded partnership ecosystem, I am confident in our go-forward strategy, and believe we are well positioned to accelerate growth in 2027.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights**


- Revenue of $18.6 million, a decrease of $8.0 million, or 30.1%, compared to Q3 2025 primarily due to a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, along with a decline in consumption-based revenue across our talent acquisition solutions.
- Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) of $55.9 million, down 12.6% from Q3 2025, principally due to the loss of iHeart Radio and lower subscription revenue across our talent acquisition solutions.
- Software Products and Services revenues of $11.7 million, a decrease of $8.7 million, or 42.7%, year over year.
- Managed Services revenue of $6.9 million, an increase of $0.7 million, or 11.3%, year over year.
- GAAP gross profit of $11.0 million, a decrease of $5.3 million, or 32.7%, year over year; GAAP gross margin of 59.1% as compared to 61.4% in Q3 2025, as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.
- Non-GAAP gross profit of $12.4 million, a decrease of $5.8 million, or 32.0%, year over year; non-GAAP gross margin of 66.5% as compared to 68.3% in Q3 2025, as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.
- Operating loss of $19.4 million, an increase of $1.2 million, or 6.9%, year over year, driven by the decrease of $5.4 million in GAAP Gross Profit and a $1.1 million increase in restructuring expenses, offset by an over $3.0 million improvement in operating expenses from our restructuring efforts through Q3 and a $1.8 million improvement in non-cash depreciation and amortization.
- Net loss of $19.2 million, an improvement of $10.1 million, or 34.5%, year over year driven primarily by an $8.4 million decrease in other expense, largely as a result of an $8.0 million loss on revaluation of the Veritone One earnout receivable in the third quarter of 2025.
- Non-GAAP net loss of $10.7 million, an increase of $2.5 million, or 31.2%, year-over-year principally driven by a decline in year over year Non-GAAP Gross Profit due to the mix of revenue in Q3 2026 as compared to Q3 2025, partially offset by a decrease in operating expenses.


**Year to Date 2026 Financial Highlights**


- Revenue of $63.1 million, a decrease of $9.1 million, or 12.6%, year over year.
- Software Products and Services revenues of $42.2 million, a decrease of $9.4 million, or 18.3%, year over year primarily due to a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, along with a decline in consumption-based revenue across talent acquisition solutions.
- Managed Services revenue of $20.9 million, an increase of $0.3 million, or 1.4%, year over year.
- GAAP gross profit of $37.6 million, a decrease of $8.1 million, or 17.7%, year over year; GAAP gross margin of 59.6% as compared to 63.2% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.
- Non-GAAP gross profit of $41.5 million, a decrease of $8.1 million, or 16.4%, year over year; non-GAAP gross margin of 65.8% as compared to 68.7% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.
- Operating loss of $61.0 million, an increase of $2.2 million, or 3.7%, year over year, driven by the decrease of $8.1 million in GAAP Gross Profit and a $5.7 million increase in restructuring expenses, offset by an over $7.0 million improvement in operating expenses from our restructuring efforts through Q3 and a $4.4 million improvement in non-cash depreciation and amortization.
- Net loss of $60.8 million, an improvement of $14.8 million, or 19.5%, year over year driven principally from lower interest expense.
- Non-GAAP net loss of $32.5 million, an increase of $4.9 million, or 17.5%, year-over-year principally driven by a decline in year over year Non-GAAP Gross Profit driven by the decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to 2025, partially offset by a decrease in operating expenses.


**Convertible Notes Exchange**


On November 13, 2026, we entered into privately negotiated exchange agreements with certain holders of our Old Convertible Notes. Pursuant to the exchange agreements, on November 13, 2026, we exchanged $38.7 million principal amount of Old Convertible Notes for (i) $38.7 million principal amount of New Convertible Notes and (ii) an aggregate of 1.6 million shares of our common stock. The New Convertible Notes mature on December 15, 2026 and are guaranteed by the Company’s U.S. subsidiaries. The New Convertible Notes are convertible into shares of our common stock at the same conversion rate as the Old Convertible Notes and, with the exception of the maturity date, the addition of subsidiary guarantees and a limitation on the incurrence of indebtedness, the New Convertible Notes have substantially the same terms as the Old Convertible Notes. The $6.8 million remaining aggregate principal amount of Old Convertible Notes will be paid upon maturity on November 16, 2026.


**Commitment Letter for Senior Secured Term Loan**


On November 15, 2026, we entered into a commitment letter (the “Commitment Letter”) with BTC to provide us with a new $40.0 million senior secured first lien term loan (the “Term Loan”), subject to certain terms and conditions set forth in the Commitment Letter. The Term Loan will bear interest, at our option, at (i) a base rate equal to the greatest of 3.00%, the Wall Street Journal federal funds rate plus 0.50%, one-month Term SOFR plus 1.00% and the prime rate, in each case plus an applicable margin of 8.25%, or (ii) Adjusted Term SOFR plus an applicable margin of 9.25%, with Term SOFR subject to a 2.00% floor. Adjusted Term SOFR will include adjustments equal to (i) 0.11448% for base rate loans and Term SOFR loans with a 1-month tenor and (ii) 0.26161% for Term SOFR loans with a 3-month tenor. The Term Loan will mature three years following the closing date, and, beginning after the first anniversary of the closing date, will amortize at a rate of 7.5% per year, payable quarterly, with the remaining principal due at maturity. Voluntary prepayments will be subject to a prepayment premium of 3.0% in year one, 2.0% in year two and 1.0% in year three; mandatory prepayments will not be subject to such premium. The Term Loan also will be subject to customary mandatory prepayments, including from 50% of excess cash flow and 100% of certain asset sale, debt-incurrence and extraordinary-receipt proceeds.


The Term Loan is subject to negotiation of a mutually acceptable credit or loan agreement and other mutually acceptable definitive documentation, which will include certain representations and warranties, affirmative and negative covenants, financial covenants, events of default and collateral and guarantee agreements that are customarily required for similar financings. The Term Loan will be guaranteed by substantially all of our existing and future subsidiaries and secured by substantially all assets of the loan parties, subject to customary and specified exceptions. Additionally, funding of the Term Loan is subject to the Company obtaining an additional $25 million in financing. We are in discussions with certain parties, including our largest stockholders, for a potential financing to meet such condition. The documentation governing the Term Loan has not been finalized and, accordingly, the actual terms may differ from the descriptions in the foregoing summary of the Commitment Letter.


We expect to use a portion of the proceeds from the Term Loan Facility and additional financing to repay the New Convertible Notes at maturity in December 2026 and the remainder for corporate and operating purposes.


**About Our Total New Bookings and Sales Pipeline**


Our total new bookings represents the total fees payable during the full contract term for new contracts received in the quarter (including fees payable during any cancellable portion and an estimate of license fees that may fluctuate over the term), excluding any variable fees under the contract (e.g., fees for cognitive processing, storage, professional services and other variable services). Our sales pipeline represents revenue we expect to receive based on the total fees payable during the full contract term for contracts that we believe have a high probability of closing in the next three to twelve months. We include in our sales pipeline fees payable during any cancellable portion and an estimate of license fees that may fluctuate over the term and we do not include any variable fees under the contract (e.g., fees for cognitive processing, storage, professional services and other variable services) and any fees payable after contract renewals or extensions that are at the discretion of our customer. Many of our contracts require us to provide services over more than one year and may include professional fees required to enable our technology in certain environments we do not host or have direct control over. In some cases, our customers may have the ability to terminate our agreements on short notice and our pipeline does not consider the potential impact of any early termination. No assurance can be given that we will ultimately realize our full sales pipeline.

*(1)*


*“Total Software Products & Services Customers” includes Software Products & Services customers as of the end of each respective quarter set forth above with net revenues in excess of $10 during the last month of the quarter and also excludes any customers categorized by us as trial or pilot status. Management uses Total Software Products & Services Customers and we believe Total Software Products & Services Customers is useful to investors because it more accurately reflects our total customers for our Software Products & Services.*


*(2)*


*“Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” represents an annualized calculation of monthly recurring subscription-based SaaS revenue during the last month of the applicable quarter for all Total Software Products & Services Customers. Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS) is useful to investors because it provides annual recurring subscription-based SaaS revenues as compared to consumption-based revenues and the split between the two allows us to delineate between predictable recurring SaaS revenues and more volatile consumption-based revenues, including VDR.*


*(3)*


*“Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption)” represents the trailing twelve months of all non-recurring and/or consumption-based revenue for all active Total Software Products & Services customers. Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption)” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption) is useful to investors because Annual Recurring Revenue provides a calculation of our trailing twelve months of consumption-based revenue from Total Software Products & Services Customers, which as noted above, excludes customers with insignificant revenue and customers on trial or pilot status. We believe the split between subscription-based SaaS revenue and consumption-based revenue allows us to delineate between predictable recurring SaaS revenues and more volatile consumption-based revenues, including VDR.*


*(4)*


*“Annual Recurring Revenue” represents the sum of “Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” and “Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption).” Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue is useful to investors because it provides our revenue from Total Software Products & Services Customers, which as noted above, excludes customers with insignificant revenue and customers on trial or pilot status.*


*(5)*


*“Total New Bookings” represents the total fees payable during the full contract term for new contracts received in the quarter (including fees payable during any cancellable portion and an estimate of license fees that may fluctuate over the term), excluding any variable fees under the contract (e.g., fees for cognitive processing, storage, professional services and other variable services).*


*(6)*


*“Gross Revenue Retention” represents a calculation of our dollar-based gross revenue retention rate as of the period end by starting with the revenue from Software Products & Services Customers as of the three months in the prior year quarter to such period, or Prior Year Quarter Revenue. We then deduct from the Prior Year Quarter Revenue any revenue from Software Products & Services Customers who are no longer customers as of the current period end, or Current Period Ending Software Customer Revenue. We then divide the total Current Period Ending Software Customer Revenue by the total Prior Year Quarter Revenue to arrive at our dollar-based gross retention rate, which is the percentage of revenue from all Software Products & Services Customers from our Software Products & Services as of the year prior that is not lost to customer churn.*

**Business Highlights**


- Expanded partnership ecosystem to include Box and integrated Veritone Redact into Getac Video Suite to help public safety agencies streamline redaction of sensitive information from video, audio, documents, and images.
- Introduced several prominent and new products and services, including Broadbean Career Sites, DMH Fusion, Veritone Video Intelligence, and expanded AI-assisted managed services in Public Sector.
- Closed 208 commercial enterprise software and licensing contracts including agreements with A&E Networks, United States Tennis Association, Australian Radio Network, and New York Public Radio.
- Closed 184 public sector contracts from new and existing customers across federal, state, and local agencies.
- Closed 564 Broadbean software and recruitment media services agreements, inclusive of traditional and programmatic media executions.
- Completed next phase of restructuring, delivering over $18.0 million in annualized cost reductions since June 2026, or approximately 18% of annual operating expenses as compared to the trailing 12 months ended June 30, 2026.
- Targeting additional cost reductions of $2.0 million to $7.0 million, representing total annualized operating expense reductions of approximately 20% to 25%, by the end of fiscal 2026.
- Completed the exchange of $38.7 million principal amount of Old Convertible Notes for $38.7 million principal amount of New Convertible Notes and an aggregate of 1.6 million shares of common stock.
- Entered into a commitment letter with BTC in connection with up to a $40.0 million senior secured term loan subject to, among other conditions, obtaining an additional $25.0 million in financing.
- On September 30, 2026, entered into an agreement to sell 20,000,000 shares of common stock at $0.75 per share in a registered direct offering, for net proceeds of approximately $13.8 million after placement agent fees and offering expenses.


**Financial Results for Three Months Ended September 30, 2026**


Delivered third quarter revenue of $18.6 million, a decrease of $8.0 million from $26.6 million in the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to a decrease in revenue generated from Software Products & Services, as a result of a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, and to a lesser extent from a decline in consumption-based revenue across talent acquisition solutions. Partially offsetting the decrease in VDR revenue was an increase in Managed Services of $0.7 million, or 11.3% year over year, driven by increases in both representation and content licensing services.


GAAP gross profit of $11.0 million decreased by $5.3 million from $16.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 driven primarily by a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, with GAAP gross margin of 59.1% decreasing 230 bps from 61.4% in the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5% as compared to 68.3% in the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of 184 bps as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.


Operating loss of $19.4 million as compared to $18.2 million in the third quarter of 2025, a decline of $1.2 million, driven by the decrease of $5.4 million in GAAP Gross Profit and a $1.1 million increase in restructuring expenses, offset by an over $3.0 million improvement in operating expenses from our restructuring efforts through Q3 and a $1.8 million improvement in non-cash depreciation and amortization.


Net loss of $19.2 million decreased from $29.2 million for the third quarter of 2025 principally due to an $8.4 million decrease in other expense, largely as a result of an $8.0 million loss on revaluation of the Veritone One earnout receivable in the third quarter of 2025 and a reduction in interest expense of $2.6 million as the result of the retirement of the Company’s senior secured term loan in November 2025 and the partial repayment of our Old Convertible Notes in November 2025. Non-GAAP net loss of $10.7 million increased by 31.2%, or $2.5 million, from a net loss of $8.2 million for the third quarter of 2025 primarily due to the $5.8 million decrease in Non-GAAP Gross Profit, offset by a year over year improvement in operating expenses as the result of our restructuring efforts through Q3 2026.


Total Software Products & Services Customers of 2,775 as of September 30, 2026 decreased by 8.1% compared to September 30, 2025. This decline was principally due to fewer consumption-based customers across our talent acquisition solutions. Annual Recurring Revenue of $55.9 million decreased $8.0 million from $63.9 million in Q3 2025 principally driven by the loss of iHeart Radio and lower subscription revenue across our talent acquisition solutions, partially offset by an increase of $0.9 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption).


**Financial Results for Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026**


During the nine months ended September 30, 2026 delivered revenue of $63.1 million, down $9.1 million from $72.3 million primarily due to a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, along with a decline in consumption-based revenue across our talent acquisition solutions. Software Products & Services revenue of $42.2 million decreased by $9.4 million, or 18.3%, year over year, principally due to a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product, along with a decline in consumption-based revenue across our talent acquisition solutions. Managed Services increased $0.3 million, or 1.4% year over year, driven by a $0.4 million increase in representation services, as growth in our VeriAds services more than offset lower influencer-based advertising revenue as a result of the more challenging macro environment, partially offset by a $0.1 million decrease in content licensing.


GAAP gross profit of $37.6 million decreased by $8.1 million from $45.7 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 primarily due to a decrease in revenue generated from our VDR product compared to the prior year period. GAAP gross margin of 59.6% decreased 366 bps from 63.2% during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue. Non-GAAP gross margin was 65.8% as compared to 68.7% during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of 291 bps primarily as a result of year-over-year declines in higher gross margin Software Products & Services revenue, resulting in a higher mix of lower gross margin Managed Services revenue.


Operating loss of $61.0 million as compared to $58.8 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, a decline of $2.2 million, driven by the decrease of $8.1 million in GAAP Gross Profit and a $5.7 million increase in restructuring expenses, offset by an over $7.0 million improvement in operating expenses from our restructuring efforts through Q3 and a $4.4 million improvement in non-cash depreciation and amortization.


Net loss of $60.8 million decreased from a net loss of $75.6 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, was principally due to a reduction in interest expense of $8.2 million as the result of the retirement of the Company’s senior secured term loan and the partial repayment of the Company’s convertible senior notes in November 2025, and a $7.2 million loss on revaluation of the Veritone One earnout receivable in the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Non-GAAP net loss of $32.5 million increased by 17.5%, or $4.9 million, from a net loss of $27.7 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025, principally driven by a year-over-year decrease in Non-GAAP gross profit, partially offset by a decrease in operating expenses.

**About the Presentation of Supplemental Non-GAAP Financial Information and Key Performance Indicators**


In this news release, the Company has supplemented its financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) with certain non-GAAP financial measures, including Non-GAAP net income (loss), Non-GAAP gross profit, and Non-GAAP gross margin. The Company also provides key performance indicators (KPI), including Total Software Products & Services Customers, Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS), Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption), Total New Bookings and Gross Revenue Retention.


Non-GAAP net income (loss) is the Company’s net income (loss), adjusted to exclude interest expense, net, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, change in fair value of earnout receivable, contingent purchase compensation expense, foreign currency impact and other, acquisition and due diligence costs, restructuring expense, severance and executive transition costs, professional fees and lender consent fees. Non-GAAP gross profit is the Company’s gross profit with adjustments to add back depreciation and amortization related to cost of revenue. Non-GAAP gross margin is defined as non-GAAP gross profit divided by revenue.


Reconciliations of each of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most closely comparable GAAP financial measure, including a breakdown of the excluded items noted above are included following the financial statements attached to this news release. These non-GAAP financial measures are not calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss), operating income (loss), gross profit, gross margin or any other financial measures so calculated and presented, nor as an alternative to cash flow from operating activities as a measure of liquidity.


The Company has provided these non-GAAP financial measures and KPI because management believes such information to be important supplemental measures of performance that are commonly used by securities analysts, investors and other interested parties in the evaluation of companies in its industry. Management also uses this information internally for forecasting, budgeting and measuring annual bonus compensation targets for executive personnel, including the Company’s named executive officers. Non-GAAP net income (loss) provides management and investors consistency and comparability with the Company’s past financial performance and facilitates period-to-period comparisons of operations, as it eliminates the effect of items that are often unrelated to overall operating performance. Non-GAAP gross profit and non-GAAP gross margin allow investors and the Company’s management team to analyze the Company’s operating performance by excluding expenses that are not directly related to the cost of providing goods and services. Other companies (including the Company’s competitors) may define these non-GAAP financial measures differently. The non-GAAP financial measures may not be indicative of the historical operating results of Veritone or predictive of potential future results. Investors should not consider these non-GAAP financial measures in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of the Company’s results as reported in accordance with GAAP.


**About Veritone**


Veritone (NASDAQ: VERI) builds enterprise AI and data solutions that transform unstructured data into actionable intelligence. Empowering customers in the commercial and public sectors, Veritone helps organizations run more efficiently, accelerate decision-making and increase profitability. Veritone’s aiWARE™ platform orchestrates a robust ecosystem of machine learning models and intelligent applications to transform data, including video, audio, and images, that power smarter models, automated workflows and measurable business outcomes. By blending human expertise with cutting-edge, ethical AI, Veritone enables customers to navigate a rapidly evolving digital landscape, delivering seamless user experiences, sustainable business models, and safeguards for intellectual property owners. To learn more, visit Veritone.com.

(1)


“Total Software Products & Services Customers” includes Software Products & Services customers as of the end of each respective quarter set forth above with net revenues in excess of $10 during the last month of the quarter and also excludes any customers categorized by us as trial or pilot status. Management uses Total Software Products & Services Customers and we believe Total Software Products & Services Customers is useful to investors because it more accurately reflects our total customers for our Software Products & Services.


(2)


“Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” represents an annualized calculation of monthly recurring subscription-based SaaS revenue during the last month of the applicable quarter for all Total Software Products & Services customers. Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS) is useful to investors because it provides annual recurring subscription-based SaaS revenues as compared to consumption-based revenues and the split between the two allows us to delineate between predictable recurring SaaS revenues and more volatile consumption-based revenues, including VDR.


(3)


“Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption)” represents the trailing twelve months of all non-recurring and/or consumption-based revenue for all active Total Software Products & Services customers. Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption)” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption) is useful to investors because Annual Recurring Revenue provides a calculation of our trailing twelve months of consumption-based revenue from Total Software Products & Services Customers, which as noted above, excludes customers with insignificant revenue and customers on trial or pilot status. We believe the split between subscription-based SaaS revenue and consumption-based revenue allows us to delineate between predictable recurring SaaS revenues and more volatile consumption-based revenues, including VDR.


(4)


“Annual Recurring Revenue” represents the sum of “Annual Recurring Revenue (SaaS)” and “Annual Recurring Revenue (Consumption).” Management uses “Annual Recurring Revenue” and we believe Annual Recurring Revenue is useful to investors because it provides our revenue from Total Software Products & Services Customers, which as noted above, excludes customers with insignificant revenue and customers on trial or pilot status.


(5)


“Total New Bookings” represents the total fees payable during the full contract term for new contracts received in the quarter (including fees payable during any cancellable portion and an estimate of license fees that may fluctuate over the term), excluding any variable fees under the contract (e.g., fees for cognitive processing, storage, professional services and other variable services).


(6)


“Gross Revenue Retention” represents a calculation of our dollar-based gross revenue retention rate as of the period end by starting with the revenue from Software Products & Services Customers as of the three months in the prior year quarter to such period, or Prior Year Quarter Revenue. We then deduct from the Prior Year Quarter Revenue any revenue from Software Products & Services Customers who are no longer customers as of the current period end, or Current Period Ending Software Customer Revenue. We then divide the total Current Period Ending Software Customer Revenue by the total Prior Year Quarter Revenue to arrive at our dollar-based gross retention rate, which is the percentage of revenue from all Software Products & Services Customers from our Software Products & Services as of the year prior that is not lost to customer churn.
